This confirms the picture clearly.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 5c38154fef70835c726a47f8d6403633acf4f2de

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** I traced the history of the four files touched by the fix commit (`EventEmail.java`, `EventsExportEventsToICal.java`, `CalendarServlet.java`, `CalendarExport.java`), since the fix consistently adds `writer.getTimezoneInfo().setDefaultTimeZone(TimeZone.getDefault())` before serializing iCalendar data in all four. I searched for when `Biweekly.write(ical).go()` was introduced (`git log -S"Biweekly.write"`) and when timezone-related code changed (`git log -S"TimeZone"`) in these files. Both searches converged on commit `5c38154f` ("Thu Sep 24 2015"), which is the closest prior touch to all four files before the fix.

**(2) The specific change:** `5c38154f` is a large third-party library upgrade commit (biweekly 0.3.3 → 0.4.3, plus many other dependency bumps). As part of adapting the code to the new biweekly API (`Version` → `ICalVersion`, `Organizer`/`Attendee` constructor changes, `ExceptionDates` constructor changes), it also **removed** every explicit timezone-setting call on `DateStart`/`DateEnd` objects, e.g.:

```java
- DateStart dstart = new DateStart(first, true); dstart.setLocalTime(false); dstart.setTimezoneId(TimeZone.getDefault().getID());
+ DateStart dstart = new DateStart(first, true);
```

These `setLocalTime(false)`/`setTimezoneId(...)` calls existed in the old (0.3.3) API to make date/time values export with the correct local timezone instead of being interpreted as UTC or floating time. In the 0.4.3 API these per-property setters were removed/changed, and the commit simply dropped the calls rather than replacing them with an equivalent mechanism — leaving no timezone information attached to the generated iCalendar output. `java.util.TimeZone` even remains imported in `CalendarServlet.java` afterward but the setters are gone.

**(3) Evidence:** The bug-fixing commit `80dcd036` restores exactly this lost behavior, but via the new 0.4.3 API's global mechanism (`ICalWriter.getTimezoneInfo().setDefaultTimeZone(...)`) instead of per-property. It touches the same four files, replacing `Biweekly.write(ical).go()` with a manual `ICalWriter` that explicitly sets the default timezone — directly undoing the regression from `5c38154f`. No other commit in the history of these files between `5c38154f` and `80dcd036` touches timezone handling (confirmed via `git log -S"TimeZone"` and `git log -S"Biweekly.write"`), so `5c38154f` is the sole commit that introduced the missing-timezone bug.

I'm confident in this identification — the removal of timezone setters and the fix's restoration of equivalent functionality line up precisely, and no intervening commit reintroduces or alters timezone logic for these export paths.

**(2) The specific change:** `5c38154f` is a large third-party library upgrade commit (biweekly 0.3.3 → 0.4.3, plus many other dependency bumps). As part of adapting the code to the new biweekly API (`Version` → `ICalVersion`, `Organizer`/`Attendee` constructor changes, `ExceptionDates` constructor changes), it also **removed** every explicit timezone-setting call on `DateStart`/`DateEnd` objects, e.g.:

```java
- DateStart dstart = new DateStart(first, true); dstart.setLocalTime(false); dstart.setTimezoneId(TimeZone.getDefault().getID());
+ DateStart dstart = new DateStart(first, true);
```

These `setLocalTime(false)`/`setTimezoneId(...)` calls existed in the old (0.3.3) API to make date/time values export with the correct local timezone instead of being interpreted as UTC or floating time. In the 0.4.3 API these per-property setters were removed/changed, and the commit simply dropped the calls rather than replacing them with an equivalent mechanism — leaving no timezone information attached to the generated iCalendar output. `java.util.TimeZone` even remains imported in `CalendarServlet.java` afterward but the setters are gone.

**(3) Evidence:** The bug-fixing commit `80dcd036` restores exactly this lost behavior, but via the new 0.4.3 API's global mechanism (`ICalWriter.getTimezoneInfo().setDefaultTimeZone(...)`) instead of per-property. It touches the same four files, replacing `Biweekly.write(ical).go()` with a manual `ICalWriter` that explicitly sets the default timezone — directly undoing the regression from `5c38154f`. No other commit in the history of these files between `5c38154f` and `80dcd036` touches timezone handling (confirmed via `git log -S"TimeZone"` and `git log -S"Biweekly.write"`), so `5c38154f` is the sole commit that introduced the missing-timezone bug.

I'm confident in this identification — the removal of timezone setters and the fix's restoration of equivalent functionality line up precisely, and no intervening commit reintroduces or alters timezone logic for these export paths.
